You are marking one part of a body paragraph in a NSW HSC Year 12 Economics extended response. The student was given a plain-English brief and the model text of the paragraph's earlier parts, and wrote ONLY the part named below. Mark it against each criterion independently: true when the student's text clearly meets it, false when it does not. Judge substance, not wording: accept equivalent phrasing, rounded but correct figures, and any accurate structure. Do not mark down a criterion for a fault that belongs to a different criterion. Do not reward material the part does not ask for. Judge each criterion on its own, as if every other criterion were fully met: a fault that belongs to one criterion (for example colloquial wording, a skipped step, missing figures) must not cost a mark on another. Work in this order. First, write 'restated': the student's text rewritten in formal economic language with exactly the same content (add no step, reason, figure or model the student did not write; drop nothing; fix no reasoning). Then judge (a), (b) and (c) on the RESTATED text, so informal wording or filler never costs a content mark. Judge the conventions on the ORIGINAL text. For each criterion write the reason first, then decide. Respond with JSON only, no prose outside it.

=====

Essay question: Evaluate the effectiveness of the strategies used by an emerging economy you have studied.
Directive verb: evaluate
Economy: Testland (emerging)
Strategy in this paragraph: Opening to trade and FDI.

Brief given to the student:
- Argument: Opening up drove fast growth.
- Counterpoint: Gains were uneven.
- Chain steps: Tariffs cut -> FDI rises -> Exports rise
- Facts: Exports doubled in 2010. Poverty fell to 5% in 2020.
- Limitation: Poverty stays high in rural areas. Growth depends on world demand.

The paragraph so far (model text shown to the student):
Topic Sentence: While opening up was highly effective for growth, gains were uneven.
Theoretical Mechanism: Tariff cuts raised FDI, lifting aggregate demand.
Evidence & Application: Exports doubled in 2010, showing FDI drove growth.

Part the student wrote: Evaluation & Limitation. Its job: Evaluates the counterpoint framed in the topic sentence: what limits the strategy, why, and how much.
Word limit: 90 words (checked separately; do not judge length).

Criteria for this part:
(a) Discusses the SAME limitation the topic sentence framed (shown in 'The paragraph so far'), through a recognised angle: inequality, environmental sustainability, exposure to external shocks, debt or dependence on external bodies, time lags. A different, unframed limitation fails this criterion even if well argued.
(b) Explains WHY that limitation reduces the strategy's effect (the economic reason), not just that it exists or what the figures are.
(c) Weighs it: says how much it limits the strategy (for example 'partially offsets', 'significantly qualifies but does not negate'), not just that it does.

Conventions (all parts):
- preciseLanguage: Uses precise economic terms in a formal register. FAILS for colloquial, flowery or everyday wording ('heaps', 'big time', 'the economy went up'), slang or idioms ('tanks', 'rubs off'), or contractions ('hasn't', 'don't').
- noPadding: No padding or filler that adds nothing ('it is important to note', 'basically', 'clearly', 'as we can see', 'in many ways').

Model Evaluation & Limitation (one acceptable version, not the only one): However, uneven gains partially offset the benefits.

Marking notes: Note evaluation: the limitation must be the one framed in the topic sentence.

Student's Evaluation & Limitation:
"""
However, the {answer} gains were uneven, so poverty stayed high in rural areas.
"""
